interest: U.S. condolences for the destroyer Sawarabi's loss, 1932.
overview: December 1932 papers on the sinking of the destroyer Sawarabi and how to convey U.S. condolences.

subfiles.about: Memorandum reporting the sinking of the Japanese destroyer Sawarabi and noting consultations on diplomatic protocol regarding condolences.
subfiles.summary: Captain Ogan reports the Sawarabi's sinking; Protocol advises no further action.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Sinking of the Japanese Destroyer Sawarabi

subfiles.about: Telegram authorizing the American Embassy in Tokyo to express condolences to the Japanese Government for the loss of the Sawarabi.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State notifies the American Embassy in Tokyo that the Japanese Naval Attaché reported the sinking of the destroyer Sawarabi with the loss of approximately ninety lives. The telegram authorizes the embassy, at its discretion, to convey the sympathy of the United States Government to the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Embassy, Tokyo Authorizing Expression of Condolences
